simple.meaning: גַּלְגַּל (galgal) is a Hebrew word meaning “a wheel ; by analogy, a whirlwind ; also dust (as whirled ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גַּלְגַּל (H1534) appears 11 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 77:19, with occurrences in Psalms, Ecclesiastes, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גַּלְגַּל (H1534) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גַּלְגַּל (H1534) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גַּלְגַּל (galgal) / H1534 is traced through Psalms 77:19, Psalms 83:14, Ecclesiastes 12:6, Isaiah 5:28 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a wheel ; by analogy, a whirlwind ; also dust (as whirled )
definitions.full: H1534. galgal גַּלְגַּל noun masculine Eccl 12:6 wheel, whirl, whirlwind (on formation compare Ba NB 204 ) — absolute ׳ג Ezek 10:2 7 t.; גַּלְגַּ֑ל Psa 83:14 ; plural with suffix גַּלְגִּלָּיו Isa 5:28 ; Jer 47:3 ; — 1 wheel , a. of war-chariot Isa 5:28 ; Jer 47:3 , also collective Ezek 23:24 ; 26:10 ; perhaps also in Ezekiel's vision 10:2 , 6 , 13 (compare wheelwork ) but compare below b. for drawing water Eccl 12:6 . 2. a. whirl (of dust or chaff) Psa 83:14 ; Isa 17:13 , simile of foes put to flight by God. b. perhaps whirling of wheels Ezek 10:2 , 6 , 13 Sm RV, but compare above c. whirlwind Psa 77:19 .

occurrences.englishText: Your way was through the sea;
As the fire that burns the forest,
before the silver cord is severed,

The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.
At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones,

He spoke to the man clothed in linen, and said, “Go in between the whirling wheels, even under the cherub, and fill both your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.”
It came to pass, when he commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, “Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim,” that he went in, and stood beside a wheel.
As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing, “the whirling wheels”.

They will come against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, and with a company of peoples. They will set themselves against you with buckler, shield, and helmet all around. I will commit the judgment to them, and they will judge you according to their judgments.

By reason of the abundance of his horses, their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of the horsemen, of the wagons, and of the chariots, when he enters into your gates, as men enter into a city which is broken open.
